title: Rotation and validation pipeline for signed driver bundles and SBOM deltas
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We currently have ad-hoc processes for rotating container images and the pinned CUDA/driver stacks used in Dedicated and Private deployments. This leads to mismatches between published SBOMs, image contents, and runtime driver versions across regions. We need an automated, auditable pipeline that: 1) produces signed driver bundle artifacts (drivers + kernel-compat metadata) and corresponding SBOM deltas, 2) publishes attested images into LTS channels with immutable tags, 3) validates compatibility against our kernel & runtime matrix, and 4) wires rollout gates (canary cohorts, perf regression checks, automated rollback triggers).

Scope: implement artifact signing & attestation, delta-SBOM generation, image rotation windows, validation jobs in CI, rollout gating logic in the release controller, and a rollback playbook. This ticket focuses on the pipeline and validation components (not the UI dashboard) and delivering a muster of automation for one initial driver family (NVIDIA 535.x) to prove the flow.
acceptance_criteria: A signed driver-bundle artifact format is defined and documented (bundle contains driver binaries, kernel-compat matrix, and a small manifest with fingerprint).
CI job that builds driver-bundle, computes SBOM delta against existing LTS image, and signs the bundle runs on merge and produces artifacts in the artifacts registry.

Image publisher consumes a signed driver-bundle and produces an immutable image tag under the LTS channel (e.g., runtime-1.20-lts-2026-02-xx) and publishes the corresponding SBOM delta file alongside the image.

Validation pipeline runs pre-rollout checks: signature verification, SBOM checksum match, kernel & CUDA compatibility tests (smoke), and tokenized perf microbenchmarks. Any failure prevents promotion to canary cohorts.
Rollout gate integrates with rollout-controller: canary cohort can be defined by region and customer tier; automated rollback triggers on perf regressions or error-rate increases beyond thresholds.
Playbook for manual rollback and emergency pinning is documented in Confluence with links to the image tags, signatures, and monitoring dashboards.
All artifacts and publishing steps are auditable with event IDs logged to the release audit stream.

Add signing step in artifact CI using KMS/HSM-backed key (owner: Infra Sec)
Create image publisher job to tag and push immutable LTS images (owner: Mateo)
Add validation pipeline: signature verify, SBOM checksum, kernel compatibility smoke, basic perf microbench (owner: Benchmarking)
Integrate rollout gates into release-controller with metric-based thresholds and canary cohort config (owner: Release Controller)
Write rollback/patch playbook and runbook (owner: SRE)
End-to-end test: prepare a canary rollout in staging and validate rollback path (owner: Release Eng)
Update release console docs to show published LTS image metadata and links to SBOM deltas (owner: Docs)
Security review and key rotation plan sign-off (owner: Security)
Postmortem template for any failed rollouts and incident summarization hook (owner: Eng Ops)
notes: 2026-01-11: Kickoff meeting — decided on CycloneDX as base SBOM format and to publish SBOM deltas instead of full SBOMs to save storage and surface only changed files.
2026-01-15: Security prefers KMS-backed asymmetric signing with artifact attestations recorded in Rekor-like transparency log. Will prototype with the existing HSM access.
2026-01-20: Benchmarking owner suggested a short microbench (latency p50/p95 token-gen and GPU util snapshot) as pre-rollout checks to catch performance regressions introduced by driver updates.

2026-01-26: Identified kernel version permutations for our current fleet (ubuntu-20.04, ubuntu-22.04, rhel-8). Need a minimal compatibility matrix; will initially gate against the top 2 kernels used by Dedicated customers.
2026-01-29: Agreed to include 'cohort tagging' in image metadata so the console can filter LTS images by region/cohort eligibility.
2026-02-02: CI prototypes produce signed bundles; initial tests show a 12s sign/attest step due to HSM latency — we will batch sign operations and cache attestations for repeated publishes.
2026-02-03: Validation job flakiness observed in kernel-compat smoke on ubuntu-20.04; investigating kernel headers mismatch in the staging runner.
